findings.claim: Requirement says all generated code should be decorated, but the change only decorates formatters, resolvers and nested helper classes, and only on non-netstandard2.0/non-.NET Framework targets. Generated code compiled on netstandard2.0/net framework is not excluded, so the README documents a gap. The guard may be deliberate (derived criterion: attribute must exist or be conditionally emitted), but coverage skew remains on those targets. Also the README claims 'All generated formatters and resolvers' while GeneratedCode/other emitted types (e.g. partial nesting types) are not covered.

receipt_plan.detail: Read the templates: nesting partial types emitted by TransformUtilities.EmitNestingTypesAndNamespaces carry no attribute, and netstandard2.0/NETFRAMEWORK consumers get none; compare with the 'All generated code' acceptance criterion.

findings.claim: TransformUtilities change from "{" to "{\r\n" for constrained nesting types is a behavioral/formatting change unrelated to the attribute; it alters generated output for nested generic types with constraints, a recently churned area, with no explanation in requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests and inspect snapshots for nested constrained generic types to confirm only newline changes and still compile; cite [L4] as recent churn.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditionally emit [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] (guarded by #if for netstandard2.0/NETFRAMEWORK) on all generated formatters, resolvers and their helper classes, with no setting.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Same attribute emission but add an opt-out setting (e.g. a MessagePackGeneratorOptions/property) to disable it, and/or also decorate every generated type including nesting partial types, so that coverage exclusion applies broadly rather than only to formatter and resolver types.
